newsitem.title: CHINA: China must control rubber imports - newspaper.
newsitem.headline: China must control rubber imports - newspaper.

text.p: A Chinese newspaper on Monday called for controls on rubber imports to prevent a glut on the domestic market.

China ought to limit imports to about 400,000 tonnes of rubber this year due to strong levels of imports in 1996 and existing stockpiles of about 200,000 tonnes, the China Chemical Industry News said.
Sluggish demand from ailing domestic firms was another factor contributing to the need for import curbs, it said.
The newspaper is published by the Ministry of Chemical Industry.

China's imports of natural rubber, including latex, in the first 11 months of last year reached 470,000 tonnes, up 67.9 percent from the same 1995 period, customs figures show. Imports of synthetic rubber, including latex, in January-November were 324,759 tonnes, up 18.2 percent from the same 1995 period.
Domestic demand in 1997 would be 1.68 million tonnes, up 5.0 percent, or 80,000 tonnes, from 1996, the newspaper said.
China's rubber production was forecast at 1.05 million tonnes, including 430,000 tonnes of natural rubber and 620,000 tonnes of synthetic rubber, it said.
Domestic rubber prices dropped sharply in 1996 and were unlikely to rebound in the first quarter of this year, the newspaper said.
The spot domestic price for rubber dropped to 13,000 yuan ($1,566) per tonne last September from 14,500-15,000 yuan per tonnes at the end of last June, it said.
